reviews.title: Great App! Few Suggestions
reviews.text: This is a great app if you want an app limit and need to be studying more! It would be great if you could reference (in a folder or tab) of all your starred questions so you can look at/review them. I use the notes section for each question to basically copy all the important info/key points I learned from the answer explanation. Maybe an ability to copy or shared the text would be easier (than screenshotting and having it convert it text in usually two separate sections because it cuts off). Other than that, love the MCAT Questions pack and excited to see more topics and how devs expand the selection. Thanks!

reviews.title: Fantastic idea
reviews.text: This is a great idea! I love this concept, it’s genuinely helpful at helping me study for my AP world exams, while still not feeling like I am being forced to be off of my phone. And an answer being required every 5 minutes is really helpful to build habits of shorter screen time

reviews.title: It’s Helpful

reviews.title: Great for scrollers
reviews.text: I really liked that this app stopped me from doom scrolling. I set it for 5 minute reminders, which would then interrupt the apps of my choosing. This gave me consistent study material throughout the day without me having to go out of my way. I used other study materials as well but I would give credit to this app for keeping me focused and helping me pass the NCLEX.

reviews.title: Great concept with poor premium pricing model
reviews.text: I really enjoy the concept of the app and using it feels great. However the features locked behind a premium version that cost $9.99 PER MONTH is kind of disappointing. I hope the developer shifts some of the features to the free version or at the very least lowers the subscription to a more reasonable price.

reviews.title: Amazing concept but some suggestions
reviews.text: This app is very well designed and has an amazing concept. As someone just starting to study for the MCAT, I appreciate how the app already has built in modules that cover each section and don’t require me to research myself. However, the default 5 minute timer gets very annoying very quickly to the point it’s counterintuitive because I just end up clicking the “turn off for 30 mins / 1 hr” button on the homepage. I wish there was a way to customize the timer without paying a subscription, maybe a default of 10 minutes instead or an auto-learning/custom algorithm that blocks the app for different durations at different times of the day. Or a timer like 30 minutes the first time, then 10 minutes, then 5 mins. That’s more realistic as sometimes we do just need a break. Not sure if these features are already available, just with the paid version though.

reviews.title: honestly changed my life
reviews.text:
i am an avid doomscroller and also a pre-PA student with adhd. this app genuinely has been the best decision ive made this year. it feels so rewarding to get an MCAT question right (even tho im personally not going to take the MCAT) and reduce my instagram usage at the same time. i highly recommend for students or anyone wishing to decrease their time on social media. i love the pause option for nights im not doing work or during my lunch break! please never get rid of the free version. if i had more money id pay for the pro version because thats how much this app genuinely benefits me. 

it will change your life! do it!

reviews.title: Helpful & effective!

While getting set up was a little intimidating, once you get started, it’s really helpful! It helps me keep track of my doomscrolling habit, and it’s a really nice way to review content and concepts. Great app

reviews.title: scroll for 5 mins
reviews.text: downloaded this to help me learn some vocab every time i go to scroll, i’m going to scroll anyways why not learn?, doesn’t tell you that unless you pay for premium it only unlocks the app for 5 mins before you have to answer another question and so on. immediately deleted, great idea but i’d like to scroll for more than 5 mins.

reviews.title: Great until it wasn’t
reviews.text: For a few days, this app was everything I’d hoped it’d be. But turns out that that’s just the free trial of the paid version, of which the app is basically useless without. I’d be interested in trying it again if this got resolved, but until then I can’t recommend it.

reviews.title: A big fan of this work in progress
reviews.text: I love this app! The developer is clearly working very hard on this and I use it a lot. That being said, the multiple choice can present some challenges on here for me in terms of memorizing the beginning of the answer/question and it would be really cool to see some short answer or jeopardy style questions to facilitate some deeper learning (maybe thats just me though 😂) Theres a good range of topics that already have questions decks and you can import your own too! I was a little bummed that I no longer saw NCLEX questions but otherwise fantastic so far. I pay for premium and feel its worth the (quite low) cost :)

reviews.title: Helping the doomscrolling
reviews.text: So happy I found this. It is really just what you need to help you stop doomscrolling and actually think about your goals and get back to studying.

reviews.title: Paywall???
reviews.text: After about a week, the app suddenly limited me to one puzzle per hour and locked me out completely, I couldn’t even leave the payment screen to use the rest of the app. This wasn’t mentioned when I downloaded it. I understand needing to monetize, but springing a hard paywall on users with no warning, and trapping them on the payment screen with no way out, is just bad way to do it.

Highly recommend- though you may want to have another more traditional study plan to supplement :) happy studying!

reviews.title: Answer choices
reviews.text: Great app! I suggest that when reading incorrect answers, instead of reading a large paragraph, it could be separated by answer choices A, B, C, and D, explaining why each is right or wrong.

reviews.title: 2nd Uworld

reviews.title: Good App with One Downside
reviews.text: I really like this app and it teaches a lot of randomized MCAT questions. I like the setup and it shows you how many you got right vs how many you got wrong and explains it VERY well and shows you what subjects you need the most help in, HOWEVER. This app is not truly a free app. After consistently playing you are paywalled to practice questions. You have an hour cooldown to answer 1 question and have to pay for the premium subscription to continue studying. This also means your apps stay locked for an hour unless you pay extra… so it defeats the purpose of the app. I’m not sure if this is because I primarily use the app for studying as opposed to a doom-scroll blocker but yeah.
